description: Config file layout version. Required in project files (a missing field is read as 1 with a warning). `sealmark config migrate` upgrades older files.
Display name of the server under test. When not set, it is taken from the server's command (or the host of its url); `my-server` is only the fallback.
Version of the server under test as you know it (reported next to the version the server announces).
Profile to start from: standard, quick, ci, strict, paranoid, or a name defined under `profiles`.
User-defined profiles: a name maps to a partial config with an optional `extends`. Project-level settings such as server cannot appear inside a profile.
Program that starts the MCP server. Alone it is a stdio server; with url, Sealmark starts it, waits for url to answer, tests it and stops it.
Arguments for command. Placeholders such as {dsn}, {sandbox} are filled by the harness. Replaces, never appends.
Environment variables for the server. Values under secret-looking names are redacted in reports.
URL of a Streamable HTTP server. Alone it must already be running; with command, Sealmark starts it and waits for this URL.
Seconds to wait for a server started with command + url to answer on url (default 60). A server that does not answer in time fails the run with its last output.
HTTP headers sent to the server (url transport). Values under secret-looking names are redacted.

The server takes no root argument and works in its own working directory: the fs pack treats that directory ({sandbox}) as the allowed root, so every path probe runs and a server that reads or writes any path fails the escape checks. Use it for a path server you cannot give a {sandbox} argument. Not locked: it only adds coverage, so a STANDARD run stays STANDARD.

Files written inside the sandbox before the server starts, as { path, content }. path must start with {sandbox} or {sandbox_home}; content may use harness placeholders and ${VAR}, never {dsn}. File only.

Tools that take a SQL string, as { tool, arg } (optional role: reader|writer|unknown, shape: string|array, args: { <parameter>: <string|number|boolean> } for the tool's other required parameters, which a placeholder cannot satisfy). Auto-detected when omitted. A list adds tools and corrects arguments; it never hides a detected tool (use tools.exclude for that), and a detected writer stays a writer.
Which entry of `servers` to run: a name or `all`. Empty runs every declared server.
Packs to run. Removing a standard pack makes the run CUSTOM; adding one (exec, custom) does not. exec only runs with --active.
Seconds the cap and timeout probes wait before a call counts as running too long (flag --timeout-probe).

A SELECT that runs for a long time, used instead of pg_sleep when a server refuses pg_sleep. Must be a SELECT. null keeps the built-in probe.

Seconds a runaway query may run before sqlite-timeout fails. null uses timeout_probe_sec.

Most tools robust-input will probe.
Size in MiB of the file fs-size-cap asks the server to read.
Largest response in MiB that still passes fs-size-cap (standard 16).

Parent directory for the disposable sandbox. null uses the OS temp directory.
Keep the sandbox after the run (--keep-sandbox).
Start the server with a built-from-scratch environment instead of inheriting yours.
Variable names copied from your environment into the scrubbed one (for example HTTP_PROXY).
Seconds before one pack is abandoned and reported inconclusive (--pack-timeout).
Size cap of the sandbox directory in MiB; a probe that exceeds it is aborted and fails.
Glob patterns of tool names to probe, evaluated before exclude. A higher layer replaces the list (it is not mergeable: a catch-all default could never be narrowed by appending).
Glob patterns of tool names never to probe (listed under not covered). Appends across layers.
Per-tool classifier overrides: { tool: { class, params } }. An override always wins and is printed.
Milliseconds to wait for the server to start and answer initialize (--connect-timeout, in seconds).
Milliseconds before an ordinary tool call counts as timed out.
Milliseconds before a verdict probe counts as timed out.
No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a server start.
No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a control call.
No longer used and ignored: servers run one after another.
No longer used and ignored: packs run one after another (they share observers).
A URL the harness may fetch through the server as a control, so a no-hit, no-refusal result can pass instead of staying inconclusive.
Allow probes that need DNS resolution (127.0.0.1.nip.io).
Force the embedded-database engine instead of detecting it from {sqlite_path} / {duckdb_path}. Setting it makes the run CUSTOM (it can switch the sqlite pack off).
false (--no-embedded) disables the embedded Postgres. null starts it when the db pack needs it.
Superuser DSN of an existing Postgres to seed instead of the embedded one (--pg). Needs --yes. Treated as a secret.

Kind of the harness-owned upstream stub the server's backend is pointed at through {upstream}. http starts a loopback stub that records every request the server forwards (flag --upstream). null starts none. The stub needs a server Sealmark starts, and the server must use {upstream} in command, args, env, url, headers or files.

Scripted replies of the upstream stub, tried in order: { id?, match?: { method?, path?, body?, header? }, reply }. match values are regular expressions (method is exact); an entry without match answers everything. reply needs exactly one of body, json or bytes, plus optional status, headers and delay_ms. {upstream_token} in a reply body becomes a fresh marker per occurrence.
What the upstream stub answers when no `responses` entry matches.
Header the upstream-credential check reads the forwarded credential from (compared case-insensitively).
Largest request body in KiB the upstream stub records; the rest is cut and marked truncated.

Token the harness sends as caller A wherever the server config says {bearer} or {bearer:a}. null mints one per run. Set it when the server validates tokens it did not issue. ${VAR} is read from the environment. Treated as a secret: redacted in config show and in reports (flag --identity-a).
Token the harness sends as caller B ({bearer:b}). null mints one per run. Must differ from identities.a. Treated as a secret (flag --identity-b).

Tools that take an identifier the server is meant to restrict (a table, dataset, path), as { tool, param }: the scope pack sends out-of-scope forms of the identifier through each. The tool keeps its classification.
Identifiers the server may serve. An entry that ends with scope.separator is a prefix (sales.public.); any other entry is exact. Needed when scope.tools is not empty.
Identifiers the server must refuse even inside scope.allow (same syntax; deny wins).
The one character that separates the parts of an identifier (and ends a prefix entry).
Whether the server compares identifiers case-insensitively (the default) or case-sensitively. An upper-case spelling of an allowed name that is refused under insensitive is noted, never failed.
Largest LIMIT (or FETCH FIRST / TOP) the statement the server forwards may carry before sql-guard-rowcap fails. A candidate setting: unlocked.

A SELECT or WITH statement the harness sends as the control for sql-guard-statements; it must reach the upstream stub. null builds one (SELECT 1 AS sm_<token>, or a read of the first exact scope.allow entry).

Which OAuth issuer the server under test trusts. stub starts the harness's own authorization server on loopback (flag --oauth): {issuer} and {jwks} name it, and the caller identities ({bearer}, {bearer:a}, {bearer:b}) become tokens it signed for {audience}, sent as Authorization: Bearer. Point the server's issuer, JWKS URL and audience at those placeholders in server.env or server.args. external declares a server that trusts its own issuer: only the checks that need no harness-signed token run (oauth-discovery). null declares nothing.

The audience (RFC 8707 resource) the stub's tokens carry and the protected-resource metadata must name; the value of {audience}. null uses server.url in canonical form (no fragment, no trailing slash).
Scopes the server requires: the control token carries them, and oauth-scope sends a token without them, which must be refused. Empty skips the scope probe.

Serve the stub issuer over https with a throwaway CA made for this run: {issuer} and {jwks} are https:// URLs and {ca_file} is the CA's PEM file. The harness also sets SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for the server it starts (to a bundle of that CA and the public roots) unless server.env sets them. false serves plain http, which a hardened server refuses as a trust root (flag --no-oauth-tls).
The client_id claim of the tokens the stub mints.
Seconds the server may take to answer when the upstream is slow before upstream-slow fails (a little slack is added). null uses timeout_probe_sec.
Regular expressions that mark a refusal as routing the caller (naming what is available, what to use instead, that retrying will not help). Replaces the default list.
Regular expressions the server's instructions must not match (a leftover prompt, a product name). Appends across layers.
Report format printed to stdout or --out.
Several formats at once (written under output.out_dir). Empty means just output.format.
Write the report to this file instead of stdout (--out).
Directory for multi-format output.
quiet, normal, or verbose (every evidence line and probe argument).
Redact secret-looking values in reports. false (--no-redact) is for local debugging only.
Path of a report template. Templates never change the result data.
Prior JSON report to compare against (--baseline).
Write the current JSON report here for later --baseline runs (--write-baseline).

With a baseline, what decides the exit code: any (the gate and regressions, the default), regressions (regressions only), drift (breaking or notable tool-surface drift). A list: fail_on: [regressions, drift].
No longer used and ignored: whether a prompt appears depends on a terminal being attached and on --yes.
Exit 1 when a graded pack is below this letter (--fail-under). Default A: anything below an A fails. Use B, C, D or F to relax it, or null (--fail-under none) to turn the gate off.
A grade below fail_under (or a baseline regression) prints a warning and exits 0. Config errors, nothing graded and server failures still fail (--soft-fail).
Exit non-zero only for regressions against the baseline.
How --fail-under treats an inconclusive pack.
Exit code used when a critical check fails (0 keeps the 0.1 behaviour).
Plugin packs: { module, options }. Plugins run in-process with your privileges and always make the run CUSTOM. Appends across layers.
Probes: valid calls for coverage, and custom checks when an entry has `check`. Entries with `check` make the run CUSTOM.
Extra lines for the report's 'not covered' section. Appends across layers.
Allow the exec pack and active custom probes to run harness-owned programs. Only the --active flag can set it; files and environment cannot.
Confirm that --pg may drop and recreate the seed database. Only the --yes flag can set it.
